samples.summary: No test that `verifyYorkieToken` actually accepts a real service token — the whole backend-attach path is untested end to end
samples.evidence: The diff adds a third accepted token type in `verifyYorkieToken` (auth.service.ts:98-105), but `packages/backend/src/auth/auth.service.spec.ts` ('Yorkie tokens' block, lines 59-105) only round-trips `issueYorkieUserToken` and `issueYorkieShareToken`; there is no case signing with `signYorkieServiceToken(secret, ...)` and verifying it comes back as `{ typ: 'yorkie-service' }`. The two other new tests cannot substitute: `yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts` stubs `verifyYorkieToken` entirely (line 22-29) and hands the controller a pre-built `{ typ: 'yorkie-service' }` object, and `yorkie.service.spec.ts:187-190` verifies the minted token with its own bare `new JwtService()` rather than through `AuthService`. So if the constant, the signing secret (`accessSecret` vs `JWT_SECRET`) or the type check diverged, every server-side attach (v1 content endpoints, DocumentCopyService, template seed) would 401 under enforcement — the default — and the whole suite would stay green.

verdict.reason: The claimed gap is real. `verifyYorkieToken` (auth.service.ts:95-107) newly accepts `YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE`, but no test anywhere signs a service token and verifies it through `AuthService`. auth.service.spec.ts:59-105 only round-trips user and share tokens plus negative cases. yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:22-29 replaces `verifyYorkieToken` with a jest.fn and injects a pre-built `{typ:'yorkie-service'}` at line 124, so the real verify branch is mocked away. yorkie.service.spec.ts:176-191 checks the minted token with a bare `new JwtService()`, bypassing AuthService. Repo-wide greps for `'yorkie-service'`, `YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE`, `YorkieServiceTokenPayload` and `signYorkieServiceToken` show the signer has exactly one call site (yorkie.service.ts:56) and no test calls it; there is no yorkie-service-token.spec.ts. In test/, the only webhook-enforcing e2e is revision-history.e2e-spec.ts, whose enforcing case is `it.skip` (line 258) and uses a user token; every other e2e either overrides YorkieService or builds it directly with no webhook in the loop. Deleting the new clause at auth.service.ts:102 would leave the suite green while every server-side attach 401s under default-on enforcement — a user-visible break with no test standing between it and merge, which is major under the test-adequacy rubric.
